sourceEligibilityArgument.argument: All three declarations are nongeneric and have nonempty physical parameter vectors. Count-loop recognition fails for the Nat functions because their parameter vectors have more than one member, and for reverse because its result is named TailList. Their root if/match expressions are unchanged by root eta inlining. The tail-loop branch therefore handles these bodies, and successful tail recognition produces the exact public while(true) export; the general implementation route is not selected.

fuel==0, fuel-1 and all tuple operands are pure accepted intrinsic/variable/literal forms. The local nextFuel is distinct from self and all parameters. The fully supplied self call has empty type arguments and arity three. Emission evaluates the old-environment RHS [nextFuel,right,left] before the simultaneous [fuel,left,right] update, so the two state values are exchanged without sequential overwrite.

again has exactly one lambda parameter, nextAccumulator, with a direct self-call body and empty type arguments. Its call vector is [nextFuel,nextAccumulator]. Alias-prefix recognition accepts nextFuel as a variable not shadowed by the lambda; the remaining variable exactly matches its sole lambda parameter. nextFuel and again are distinct from declaration parameters, self, alias names and captured names. The one supplied actual accumulator+1 completes the recorded captured prefix to exactly the physical arity two. Thus the alias is elided and the update uses [nextFuel,(accumulator+1n)]. This does not assert recognition of a nested unary two-missing-slot alias.

TailList has no type parameters, with nil and cons(head:Nat,tail:TailList) in that order. The reverse body has exactly these two alternatives, ordered field bindings headValue/tailValue, and distinct safe binding names. The nil branch returns accumulator. The cons branch calls self with tailValue and the pure constructor expression TailList.cons(headValue,accumulator), giving exactly two arguments. The emitted transition therefore uses TailList["cons"](headValue, accumulator); no residual self call or runner implementation is necessary. The existing invalid-tag fallback remains the same Error.

The monomorphic nullary TailList.nil is the emitted value, so the host reads runtime.TailList.nil without invoking it. The two-field cons is a factory, so the host constructs each input cell with runtime.TailList.cons. These are the actual reviewed emitter conventions, not the generic List.nil factory convention.

The new IR uses the existing compiler-owned constructors/factories and the exact Model fields. The existing original-IR checker sees the same object whose declarations/layout are then inspected, emitted twice for checked/raw parity, compiled once and observed. Each new body has the declared type by its Nat operations, exact recursive signatures, exact constructor fields and exhaustive two-constructor match. The fixture equations are an ordinary induction on natural fuel or finite list length and have pure RHS computations. Only their twelve stated finite host observations are added; this is not a claim about arbitrary callbacks, all malformed carriers, allocation failures or universal source preservation.
